narrative.overview: ARCS renders at earned fidelity. Every surface is only as sharp as the evidence deserves, and it never lies about how certain it is. Clarity is not granted at load; it is earned as the fog lowers and the terrain resolves. The world is obsidian and single-theme, a dark cockpit read under pressure: calm, precise, serious play. Color is never ornament; each hue is a state. Depth is made of light, not cast shadow. The signature is the mark: a Mobius strip (the tilde extruded) rising from a fog field onto a clean gold horizon.
keyCharacteristics: Earned fidelity: four render states (SHARP / DEGRADED / GRAIN / MOIRE) that degrade legibility to match evidence.
Obsidian, single-theme, dark-cockpit; no light mode.
Semantic color: every accent is a state, used on <=10% of a screen.
Glow, not shadow: depth is luminance, not cast darkness.
Mono for instruments, serif for canon, sans for the body.
The tilde is the atomic glyph and the honesty marker.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Color is state, never decoration. Cyan is bearing, green is coherence, gold is locked, red is ruin, violet is conviction-shift, magenta is paradox. If a color would not survive being read as its state, it does not belong on the screen.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Any single signal color occupies <=10% of a screen. Rarity is the legibility.

rules.name: The Glow-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is made of light, never of cast darkness. A surface at rest is flat. Elevation is a signal-colored glow that appears as a response to state, not an ambient default.

rules.name: The Three-Voice Rule
rules.body: Mono = instrument, Sans = reading, Serif = canon. Never cross them: a proverb never renders in mono, a gauge label never in serif.

rules.name: The Graded-Legend Rule
rules.body: Mono labels use six graded tiers: as a tier rises, size increases and tracking decreases while weight holds, so a heading never reads like a field label.

dos: Do render at earned fidelity: match the surface's sharpness to the evidence (SHARP only when GREEN/LOCKED).
Do keep assessed values marked with a leading tilde and dimmed one step.
Do use color as state only, on <=10% of a screen.
Do convey depth with signal-colored glow as a response to state; keep surfaces flat at rest.
Do separate the three voices strictly: mono for instruments, sans for reading, serif for canon.
Do give every interactive element a visible cyan focus ring.
donts: Don't render SHARP on thin evidence; a coarse honest reading beats a confident fabrication.
Don't use a signal color decoratively, or let one flood the screen.
Don't use cast drop-shadows for elevation.
Don't set the wordmark or a proverb in the wrong voice.
Don't use em-dashes anywhere; prefer commas, colons, periods, or the interpunct.
